How are the SOPs, policies and work instructions created, maintained, and accessed by personnel?

Creation: drafted by the process-owner department based on applicable regulations and QMS requirements, industry practice and internal experience; reviewed by the department head and Quality Manager and approved by the Laboratory Director before release.

Maintenance: reviewed at least annually, or promptly revised upon process change or regulatory update. Each document records revision history and the reason for change. Obsolete versions are archived and clearly identified to prevent unintended use.

Access: current paper copies are signed/stamped and issued to departments; electronic copies are stored on a shared server/internal platform with role- and department-based access. Training is provided at onboarding and upon document update, with training records retained. A master list of controlled documents is maintained to ensure traceability.
How does the business assure that unintended use of obsolete documents is prevented?

For paper copies, after a new version is released the document administrator promptly retrieves all obsolete printouts from workstations and laboratories, stamps them “Obsolete”, archives them for the defined period and then destroys them. Electronic controlled documents are stored centrally on the server; after a new version is released the previous version is superseded and ordinary users cannot access or download it.
Internal audits include workplace checks to confirm that no uncontrolled or obsolete documents remain at points of use.
Are your procedures maintained by a documented revision policy?
Yes. A documented revision policy is followed. ODC-CX-33 Document Control Procedure defines revision and addition of documents:

To revise a document, the applicant completes a Document Application Form for review by the original reviewer (or the Quality Manager if the original reviewer is unavailable). After Quality Manager approval, the revised draft is reviewed by the original reviewer and approved/released by the designated approver.

To add a document, the applicant completes a Document Application Form; after approval the drafting–review–approval–release process is followed. The document administrator updates the Document Control List and the Document Issue and Retrieval Register.
Handwritten alteration of QMS documents is not permitted.
Changes shall be recorded on the revision page, identifying the change and the approver.
When a document is reissued, Quality retrieves and destroys the previous version.
After document review, the document administrator prepares the Annual Document Review Record; after approval by the document approver, revision is arranged.
Please describe the implemented Good Documentation Practices.
ODC-CX-33 Document Control Procedure — document establishment:
Document control: controlled / uncontrolled / obsolete copies are stamped accordingly to prevent misuse.
Unique identification: documents are numbered as “company abbreviation–category–serial number”; record forms add “R + sequence”.
Version control: version letters A/B/C… and revision numbers 0/1/2…; a version increment is required after nine revisions.
Segregation of review and approval: designated reviewers and approvers sign at defined document levels.
A defined interval is maintained between the approval date and the effective date.
Periodic review: documents are reviewed before the annual internal audit and revised as needed.
Record-entry rules: blue/black ink; corrections by single-line strikethrough with signature; correction fluid is prohibited.
Archive protection: periodic archiving with protection against mould, insects, rodents and fire; electronic and paper records are regarded as equivalent.
Defined retention: different record types have defined retention periods (e.g. examination raw data 6 years; tumour molecular testing records 20 years).
Controlled destruction: destruction after expiry requires application and approval, a destruction record and confidential handling.

FACILITIES MANAGEMENT
Does the business have physical facility security (access controls and alarms, fire alarms, etc.)?

Yes. Per ODC-CX-10 Facility and Environmental Management Procedure, the company is equipped with safety facilities and equipment, including emergency evacuation devices and alarm systems, readily accessible emergency showers and eyewash stations, with periodic functional verification. Access to critical areas is restricted: laboratory staff enter by access card or fingerprint; other persons enter only with authorization. Smoking is prohibited throughout the premises. The safety administrator maintains fire-fighting equipment and checks its effectiveness regularly.
Please give an overview of the facility size and structure (one or multiple buildings, main usage, etc.).

Per ODC-CX-10 Facility and Environmental Management Procedure, the facility is purpose-designed with zoned management; areas are separated by laboratory-grade fire-resistant boards/partitions of defined height and thickness.

Per ODC-AQ-34 Company Risk Assessment and Risk Control SOP, the laboratory is operated at biosafety level 2 (BSL-2). Principal use is medical laboratory testing, including throat swabs, gastric mucosa and other specimen types.
Per ODC-AQ-42 Pest Control SOP, pest-control coverage includes the laboratory perimeter, open areas and laboratory rooms.
Does the business have pest control and related contracts?
The company has established ODC-AQ-42 Pest Control SOP: the General Administration Department prepares the pest-control plan and oversees completion of pest-control activities;
Routine in-house pest-control activities are mainly performed by the General Administration Department.
Are facilities regularly inspected related to pest control, and is this documented?

Yes. Per ODC-AQ-42 Pest Control SOP, internal pest/rodent control is performed monthly. Glue-board locations are fixed, kept clean and cleared of carcasses and debris. Placement locations and quantities shall remain effective and are documented on ODC-AQ-42-R01 Pest and Rodent Control Record.
Is there control of temperature and humidity in the facility, and is this documented?

Per ODC-CX-10 Facility and Environmental Management Procedure, testing areas with temperature or humidity requirements are equipped with thermometers/hygrometers. On-duty laboratory staff record temperature/humidity daily. Freezers/refrigerators used for reagents or samples, incubators and similar equipment have thermometers or probes. A designated person assigned by the Laboratory Director records temperatures and checks the monitoring system. Records are kept on ODC-CX-10-R01 Indoor Temperature and Humidity Record.
What actions are taken if temperature/humidity is out of specification?
Per ODC-CX-10 Facility and Environmental Management Procedure:

When temperature or humidity is out of specification, prompt adjustment is required. Temperature is adjusted via HVAC; a dehumidifier is used if humidity is high and a humidifier if humidity is low. If specification cannot be restored, the departmental equipment administrator is notified to arrange maintenance; testing is stopped during repair and the Nonconformity Identification and Control Procedure is executed. For reagent/sample storage units, incubators and similar equipment, if specification cannot be restored, stored materials are transferred to other qualified units during repair. Upon detecting an excursion, the Laboratory Director is notified immediately; the quality supervisor completes the Facility and Environment Out-of-Control and Handling Record. If result quality may be affected, testing is stopped and the Nonconformity Identification and Control Procedure is applied.
Does the business have back-up power generators?
No dedicated back-up generator is installed. Dual-feed electrical supply is available (manual switchover, not automatic). Five UPS units are connected to critical equipment.

8. CHANGE MANAGEMENT
Is there a procedure in place for change management?

Change management is implemented across multiple procedures, covering documents (ODC-CX-33 Document Control Procedure), examination procedures (ODC-CX-20 Selection, Verification and Validation of Examination Procedures), IT systems (ODC-CX-30 Computer Hardware and Software Management Procedure), personnel (ODC-CX-09 Human Resource Management Procedure) and reagent suppliers (ODC-CX-14 Reagent and Consumable Management Procedure).
Is a risk-based approach implemented during the change management process?

Per ODC-CX-09 Human Resource Management Procedure, personnel/role changes require revision and approval of job descriptions; accreditation-related changes are notified to CNAS within 20 working days; retraining and reassessment are required upon role change, return after more than 6 months’ absence, or policy/procedure/technology change. The procedure does not explicitly use the wording “risk-based approach”. Per ODC-CX-10 Facility and Environmental Management Procedure, a laboratory safety risk assessment is performed annually and is re-performed when facilities change, with reference to the Risk Management Procedure. Change-triggered re-assessment reflects a risk-based approach.

Per ODC-CX-12 Equipment Management Procedure, application and approval are required before return to use after repair, storage or transfer; after fault repair, calibration, IQC, comparison or retained-sample retest is selected according to the impact on analytical performance. Status labelling is qualified / restricted use / out of service. The procedure does not explicitly use the wording “risk-based approach”.

Per ODC-CX-14 Reagent and Consumable Management Procedure, supplier changes require re-evaluation; reagents/consumables of different lots/shipments shall be verified before use; nonconforming materials are returned and used as input to supplier evaluation; quality risk of materials within 2 months of expiry is assessed before return/exchange.

Per ODC-CX-20 Selection, Verification and Validation of Examination Procedures, examination-procedure changes are approved on an Examination Procedure Change Approval Form; whether existing verification/validation protocols can be used is assessed; reagent upgrades, instrument updates and calibrator-traceability changes are verified as a new system; partial performance verification is required after events that severely affect analytical performance. The scope of verification is determined by the impact of the change, reflecting a risk-based approach.

Per ODC-CX-33 Document Control Procedure, document revision and addition follow the Document Application Form for review by the original reviewer and approval/release by the approver. Risk grading is not defined, nor are risk-based review frequency or methods specified.
Is the change management process implemented throughout the company, relating to all activities (e.g. project changes, IT changes)?

The company implements unified change control. Change management is defined in multiple procedures covering documents (ODC-CX-33 Document Control Procedure), examination procedures (ODC-CX-20 Selection, Verification and Validation of Examination Procedures), IT systems (ODC-CX-30 Computer Hardware and Software Management Procedure), personnel (ODC-CX-09 Human Resource Management Procedure) and reagent suppliers (ODC-CX-14 Reagent and Consumable Management Procedure).
Are all changes approved before execution?

Yes. All changes shall be approved by the designated approver before execution (per ODC-CX-33 Document Control Procedure; ODC-CX-20 Selection, Verification and Validation of Examination Procedures; ODC-CX-30 Computer Hardware and Software Management Procedure).
Are all changes managed in a system?

Per ODC-CX-30 Computer Hardware and Software Management Procedure, software go-live/authorization uses the Computer Software Validation Record; new/changed tests use the System New Examination Item Application Form and System Examination Item Information Change Record; access-right changes use the Information System Access Rights Record; database changes use the Database Server Maintenance, Upgrade and Change Record. However, UPS maintenance, breakdown repair and workstation rounds still use paper forms and are not fully systematized.

Per ODC-CX-09 Human Resource Management Procedure, recruitment applications and personnel changes are processed via Administrative and HR; training plans, competency assessments and personnel files are paper forms.

Per ODC-CX-10 Facility and Environmental Management Procedure, facility/environment out-of-control records, temperature/humidity records, water-quality monitoring, housekeeping checks and visitor registers are paper records.

Per ODC-CX-12 Equipment Management Procedure, equipment procurement follows OA application under the External Service and Supply Management Procedure; equipment status labelling, acceptance, repair, calibration and decommissioning/scrapping use paper forms.

Per ODC-CX-14 Reagent and Consumable Management Procedure, purchase requests go through the OA system; inbound, outbound and inventory use the “reagent and consumable intelligent management system”; paper forms are used only when the system is unavailable. 10. LABORATORY TEST SPECIFIC QUESTIONS
Samples
Is there a procedure in place for sample reception?

Yes. ODC-CX-19 Primary Sample Reception and Handling Procedure has been established, defining sample reconciliation, receipt, information entry, rejection of unsuitable samples and testing under concession.
Can you guarantee complete cold-chain custody?

Per ODC-CX-18 Primary Sample Collection and Transport Procedure, samples are transported in rigid specimen boxes under temperature control, with transport temperature recorded. Receipt includes a transport-temperature check; if temperature is out of control, impact on results is assessed. For storage, per ODC-CX-32 Emergency Preparedness Procedure, a remote real-time temperature/humidity monitoring system is in place and abnormalities are handled immediately.
Do your processes describe sample integrity checks?

Per ODC-CX-19 Primary Sample Reception and Handling Procedure, incoming samples are checked against acceptance criteria, including integrity, identification and collection time. Unsuitable samples are rejected or, after assessment, tested under concession with a documented remark in the system.
Do you have a sample identification process (accession labels, barcode, readers, re-labelling) in place?

Samples are identified by a unique 12-digit barcode, ensuring traceability from collection, receipt, transfer, distribution and examination through reporting (ODC-CX-19 Primary Sample Reception and Handling Procedure). Pathology reports use the pathology number as the unique identifier (ODC-CX-26 Examination Result Reporting Procedure).
Does your company have a procedure for sample storage and retention?
How long are samples retained following analysis?

Per ODC-SOP-CRO-01-012 Clinical Research Group Sample Reception and Handling Procedure, post-analysis sample retention follows the clinical trial protocol, ethics approval and customer requirements; samples are retained long-term until project completion.
Do you have a process in place for sample disposal?

Per ODC-SOP-CRO-01-019 Clinical Research Group Post-Examination Sample Management Procedure, samples exceeding the retention period are disposed of safely as medical waste by the respective technical groups.
Is there a temperature monitoring system?

Per ODC-CX-32 Emergency Preparedness Procedure, laboratory storage equipment is equipped with remote real-time temperature/humidity monitoring. Per ODC-CX-10 Facility and Environmental Management Procedure, each technical group performs routine temperature/humidity monitoring and recording according to instrument and reagent requirements; out-of-control conditions are handled immediately.

Is there a spill procedure in place?

Per ODC-CX-10 Facility and Environmental Management Procedure, in the event of contaminant leakage or spillage, all contaminated surfaces (benches, floors, walls, etc.) and air are disinfected according to procedure. Chemical spills are handled per the emergency process in the Safety Manual (ODC-CX-32 Emergency Preparedness Procedure).

Please describe your method validation process.

Per ODC-CX-20 Selection, Verification and Validation of Examination Procedures, the verification/validation process is: prepare a protocol (including performance characteristics and acceptance criteria) → Technical Director approval → implementation by authorized personnel with raw-data retention → draft verification/validation report → technical group leader review → Technical Director approval.
Is a validation plan and report available for each test(s)/parameter(s) performed by your laboratory?

Please explain, with rationale, when verification/validation is performed and when it is not.

Per ODC-CX-20 Selection, Verification and Validation of Examination Procedures, verification is performed: before routine use; after events that severely affect analytical performance (e.g. major instrument component failure, relocation, severe environmental loss of control); and when elements of the measuring system change (reagent upgrade, instrument update, change in calibrator traceability, etc.). Validation is required for: non-standard methods; laboratory-developed methods; standard methods used outside their intended scope; and modified validated methods.
